newsitem.title: FRANCE: ROYAL BRUNEI APPOINTS FRANCE AIR CARGO SALES AGENT.
newsitem.headline: ROYAL BRUNEI APPOINTS FRANCE AIR CARGO SALES AGENT.

text.p: Airline Management Services (AMS) said it has been appointed off-line cargo sales agent in France for Royal Brunei Airlines.

"We had been working for the airline on a trial basis for about a year and they have been satisfied enough with our performance to appoint us as their official French GSA," an AMS official told Reuters.
Royal Brunei operates a daily Boeing 767-300 passenger service between London and Brunei and twice-weekly Frankfurt-Brunei flights using the same type of aircraft.
The 767-300 can handle up to nine tonnes of cargo per flight.

"We will be operating daily trucking runs fron France to London and twice-weekly to Frankfurt and this will prepare the ground for when Royal Air Brunei goes on-line from Paris next summer with a proposed twice-weekly 767-300 service," the official said.
The airline had planned to start scheduled passenger services between Paris and Brunei in autumn 1997 but network development has been put on hold.
This follows a number of senior management changes and a launch date of mid-1998 was now envisaged, a Royal Brunei official told Reuters.
A French company, AMS, has offices at the two Paris airports, Charles de Gaulle and Orly, as well as at Mulhouse and Marseille and plans to open a new office at Lyon in 1998, the official said.
The agent's airline customers also include Air Malawi and Riga Airlines.
